Subject: Creative assets/license question + support SLA wording for marketplace listings

Hi team,

Quick ask as we prepare the AWS/Azure/GCP listing bundles for CloudPartner: we ran into a couple of license and SLA wording items the marketplace portal flagged and I want to make sure we align before we push final assets. Can you confirm the following requirements / restrictions for listing approval?

1) Logo / creative usage: we have a few modified lockups and a third-party icon set (analytics badges) included in the creative pack. Is a vendor-provided third-party icon license required to be uploaded to the portal, or is a statement from our legal counsel sufficient? I attached the icon license PDFs for reference.

2) Claim language: the listings currently include the phrase "SLA-backed low-latency inference". If the marketplace policy requires specific metrics or links to an SLA doc, tell us what the minimum required verbiage is.

3) Support window verbiage: the portal shows a required "support hours" field. Our public posture is: "Business hours (M–F, 9am–6pm PT) with optional 24x7 for Dedicated customers (separate contract)". Will that pass, or do marketplaces expect a single explicit 24x7 claim?

4) Timeline: CloudPartner is targeting go-live the week of 9/11. Please confirm any approvals that might add an extra 7–10 days so we can adjust our rollout plan.

Attachments: redwood_creative_pack_v3.zip (zip, logos + copy + preview PNGs), third_party_icon_licenses.pdf (pdf), draft_listing_copy_v2.md (md)

If you can respond with the portal acceptance checklist and any specific phrasing templates for claims/support, that would be ideal.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Partner Programs Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marketplace Listing Team <listings@aws-partner.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Creative assets/license question + support SLA wording for marketplace listings

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the details and the attachments — useful. Quick answers inline below: 

1) Third-party icons: AWS requires evidence of rights for any third-party assets used in the listing (licenses or written permission). A statement from legal is acceptable only if it explicitly references the third-party vendor and the license terms; a scanned license or PDF is preferred for audit.

2) Claim language: the marketplace compliance team asks for neutral, verifiable claims. "SLA-backed low-latency inference" is OK only if you link to the exact SLA (public page or a marketplace-facing doc) and you do not include comparative superlatives (e.g., "the lowest latency"). If you can provide a one-line metric (p99 latency for the most common config) that maps to the SLA, include it as "p99 latency ≤ Xms (see SLA)".

3) Support window: the portal has a dropdown for "Standard Support Hours"; options are "24x7" or "Business hours (local)". It is fine to select Business hours and then add a short note in the listing details that Dedicated customers have 24x7 support under separate contracts. You should not select multiple items in the dropdown — use the standard option plus the explanatory copy.

4) Timeline: typical approval takes 3–7 business days once all assets + licenses + signed listing agreement are in. If legal sign-off or license verification is needed, add another 5–10 business days.

Next steps: please upload the license PDFs to the "Supporting evidence" section on the portal, add a link to the SLA doc in the "Legal/Compliance" field, and confirm the support dropdown value. Once those are in, we can queue the listing for review.

Portal link: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/listings/12345

Regards,
Marketplace Listing Team
AWS Partner Ops
